The #703 + #707 same-window credit work retired these behaviours, so the tests that pinned them are gone or renamed. Four groups. (1) The DISPLAY split: an Anthropic reset never changes the week's boundaries, so `_apply_reset_events_to_weekrefs` and its SubWeek sibling no longer truncate the pre-credit week, re-anchor the post-credit one or synthesize a second reference. Every identifier naming a synthesized pre-credit row, a two-row credited week, a post-credit current-row disambiguation or a display start moved to the credit moment names a behaviour that no longer exists; each was rewritten in place under a name describing what the surface does now. (2) The dashboard's Bug-K pre-credit segment cache had exactly one consumer — that synthesized row — so the cache went with it. The rows for its own three real-builder parity tests are declared under the dedicated Bug-K-cache declaration below rather than here, so that each retired node is declared exactly once. (3) The MILESTONE-HISTORY index lists a credited week once instead of once per credit, with the detail grouping the week's ladders by epoch, so the tests asserting two opaque cycle entries and a per-cohort detail were rewritten around the new shape. (4) The two `test_journal_revisions` parametrizations and the six `test_quota_model_kernel` cases carry the epoch constant or the retired `weekly_credit_floors` fork in their identifiers: the epoch moved 1011 to 1012, and a manual credit is a `week_reset_events` row now rather than a floor, so both sets are collected under new identifiers. Two `test_in_place_credit_detection` cleanup cases named the 1.0pp tolerance band the evidence bracket replaced. No coverage was dropped: every group above is rewritten in the same module, and the estate's added rows are those rewrites.

The name and the docstring of `test_apply_reset_events_leaves_both_sub_weeks_alone` stated the opposite of one of its own assertions. They said every sub-week is returned as it came, while the body asserted that the pre-reset week's `end_ts` WAS rewritten - carried forward to the boundary the API's own later statement moved it to, which is the one rewrite #703 + #707 keeps. The identifier moves to a name that describes what the function does, test_apply_reset_events_never_cuts_a_sub_week_at_the_credit, and the docstring now states the surviving rewrite explicitly. The body and every assertion are unchanged, so no coverage moved with the name.

The name `test_the_accounting_anchor_stays_at_the_credit` and its docstring both asserted a claim that stopped being true one commit later. They called `TuiCurrentWeek.week_start_at` the ACCOUNTING anchor and said the range `spent_usd` covers starts at the credit, which is what spec section 6.2 forbids in two sentences: spend and budget range stays the full week, and a credited week's displayed total cost is the full week's spend. What the field really anchors is the RATE - the `$/1%` numerator, the nominal-rollover version fragment and the #620 Projects grid and Blocks panel windows - and all of that is unchanged and still asserted. The identifier therefore moves to test_the_rate_anchor_stays_at_the_credit and the docstring now states which quantities take that instant and which take the week's own start. Every assertion in the body is unchanged, so no coverage moved with the name.

The legacy conversation bridge no longer merely arms conversation_sessions_backfill_pending after declining to copy the rollup; it DERIVES the rollup from the conversation_messages it imported, through the ordered-write chokepoint, and arms nothing when that derive succeeds. Arming alone left the rollup empty and non-authoritative for the whole life of a `dashboard --no-sync` process, which emptied the browse filter's project facet and moved every rail read onto the live branch. So test_the_legacy_bridge_arms_the_backfill_rather_than_copying_the_rollup became false about its own subject, and the identifier moves to test_the_legacy_bridge_derives_the_rollup_rather_than_copying_it, which describes what the function now checks. A companion identity, test_the_legacy_bridge_leaves_the_rollup_authoritative_for_a_no_sync_reader, was added alongside it to pin the authoritativeness and the project facet.

These rows tested the same-window weekly credit model that #703 and #707 introduced and that shipped in 1.106.0. Under that model a week in which Anthropic reset the counter was reported as one row per calendar week, with the credit recorded in place and the week never re-anchored. The operator ruled that model incorrect: a reset ends one billing cycle and begins the next, and `cctally weekly` must show one row per billing cycle. Both features are reverted on this branch, so the behavior these rows assert no longer exists and the rows were removed with the code rather than retained against absent behavior. The pre-#703 tests covering cycle-anchored weeks are restored by the same revert and are live in this estate.

declarations.reason: These rows tested the dashboard Weekly panel's presentation-layer pre-credit synthesis ("Bug K") and the module-level segment cache that fed it: `BugKSegment`, `_bugk_key`, `cached_bugk_segment`, `reset_bugk_segment_state` and `reconcile_bugk_cache`. That synthesis existed because `_apply_reset_events_to_subweeks` did not split a week credited in place, so the dashboard rebuilt the missing pre-credit segment itself from its own `MIN(week_start_at)` query and its own re-fold. The applier now performs the split, which is where its twin `_apply_reset_events_to_weekrefs` has always performed it, so the credited week arrives as two ordinary SubWeek segments and the presentation-layer copy had to go in the same change: running both renders a credited week as three rows and double-counts the pre-credit cost. The code these rows exercise no longer exists. The three real-builder parity rows carried three different properties, and the replacement carries one of them. `test_bugk_segment_cache_parity` asserted that a closed pre-credit aggregate is served identically from cache and from scratch; `tests/test_dashboard_rebuild_parity.py::test_credited_week_group_a_cache_parity` carries exactly that, asserting byte-equality across cache-off, cold and warm over the same in-place-credit fixture. It does NOT carry the other two. `test_bugk_segment_cache_warm_no_refetch` asserted that a warm read does not re-fetch the closed pre-credit window, and `test_bugk_segment_cache_late_ingest_recomputes` asserted that a late ingest into that window evicts the entry and recomputes it. Neither property is specific to a credited week any more, because the Group A cache now owns the segment like any other week, so both are covered generically by the Group A suite in the same module rather than by a credit-specific row.

A rename, not a retirement. `test_subweek_and_weekref_appliers_agree_on_in_place_credit` seeded only the in-place-credit `week_reset_events` row shape, while `docs/credit-gotchas.md` described it as the tie that every change to either applier's case handling must go through. The test is now `test_subweek_and_weekref_appliers_agree_on_every_event_shape`, parametrized over all three shapes the two appliers handle — in-place credit, pre-reset truncation and post-reset shift — plus two spelling variants of the credit case. The former single case survives verbatim as the `in_place_credit` parameter, so the estate's added rows carry every assertion this row carried and four cases it did not. One of those additions found a real divergence: with the event row written in a non-UTC offset, `_apply_reset_events_to_weekrefs` matched raw column text and recognized nothing where `_apply_reset_events_to_subweeks` matched parsed instants and split the week.

A rename, not a retirement. The `WeeklyPanel` footer counted its rows as weeks, which is false now that a week Anthropic credited in place supplies two rows: the panel read "4w total" over four billing cycles, and would read "12w total" over twelve cycles spanning nine calendar weeks. Claude now counts in the same noun Codex already used, so the assertion and the case title both say cycles. The case is otherwise unchanged and appears in the estate's added rows as `renders the whole-window footer total (all 4 cycles)`.
